newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa slips through 899 support to new low.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa slips through 899 support to new low.

text.p: London cocoa futures slipped below crucial support at 899 basis March on Friday on origin and light fund sales, but the damage was limited by extended Christmas holidays.
"A lot of industry buyers are away. In the meantime you're getting origin selling. We're finding better selling than buying," said one trader.
Some trade houses sold early on, anticipating sterling's strength against the French franc would trigger some hedging from African origins like Ivory Coast which trade in francs.

After a brief hesitation, the benchmark March contract gave in to origin pressure and took out 899 -- a double bottom on technical charts -- falling to a fresh nine-month low of 893 stg a tonne. It closed slightly higher at 895, down five on the day.
"As it went through 899 we had some light fund selling. But it was very easily absorbed," said the trader citing trade short-covering at the lows.
Other contracts lost up to four stg at midday and volume totalled 1,298 lots -- relatively active considering many players have taken the day off to bridge Christmas holidays with a long weekend.
Turnover included 200 lots of crosses on March and AA-type business. March/May stood at 20 stg.
Technical analysts placed the next support level at 883 stg on the second-month continuation chart. But New York was due unchanged, and traders said a weaker dollar should hold the market there.
On fundamental news, dock workers at Ivory Coast's main port of Abidjan ended their strike and resumed work on Thursday.
